items.title: Introducing OpenDocRouter: Call any OCR model in a single line of code
items.summary: OpenDocRouter turns PDFs and images into clean markdown using the latest frontier and open-source OCR models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, MinerU2.5-Pro and PaddleOCR-VL. Switching models means changing one parameter. You don't touch prompts, rate limits or deployments. Every model is benchmarked on ParseBench for both quality and cost. Turn on layout and any model returns grounded bounding boxes with the same set of layout classes, even models that can't do this natively. Billing is pay-per-token, starting as low as $0.80 per 1,000 pages, and you aren't charged for pages that fail. ▶ Try it: https://www.opendocrouter.ai/ ▶ Docs: https://www.opendocrouter.ai/docs ▶ Models + benchmarks: https://www.opendocrouter.ai/models ▶ Launch blog: https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-opendocrouter

items.title: AI Fooled the Deepfake Expert
items.summary: In episode 1033 of the SuperDataScience podcast, @JonKrohnLearns discusses with Prof. Jeff Hancock, Stanford University, how even a deepfake expert like himself was fooled by AI hallucinations. He recounts a painful personal experience where AI inserted made-up references into his work, leading to reputational damage and a judge questioning the credibility of his entire declaration. This incident highlights the challenges and risks associated with AI, even for those with extensive expertise in the field.

items.title: AI Models vs. AI Decisions: What Enterprises Need to Know
items.summary: Over the past 12 months, enterprise AI strategy has shifted from simply building models and deploying experimental agents to integrating AI directly into core business processes that drive measurable ROI. As organizations face ballooning token costs from over-relying on frontier LLMs for routine tasks, enterprise leaders are pivoting toward Small Language Models (SLMs), building semantic ontology layers to give agents enterprise context, and implementing AI-native harness engineering for production-ready code. In this interview recorded live at Cypher 2026, Senior Tech Journalist Supreeth Koundinya sits down with Rashmi Tambe, VP & Head of AI Product Engineering at Tredence. She breaks down the evolving role of developers from "vibe coding" to harness engineering, why the enterprise data context problem is becoming a semantic/ontology challenge, deploying SLM gateways to optimize token spend, returning to classic machine learning fundamentals, and measuring success through business outcomes rather than agent count. items.title: PayTM CEO on India's AI Future: Why Being a User Is Being a Loser
items.summary: While India handles over 24 billion UPI transactions monthly, a testament to domestic tech execution. Paytm Founder & CEO Vijay Shekhar Sharma argues that the country is risking its future by settling for being mere "AI users" and "sloppy wrapper writers" rather than building and owning sovereign foundation models. Speaking on Day 1 of Cypher 2026, Sharma challenges the belief that India lacks the capital or technical capability to own its intelligence, calling for a shift from consuming foreign AI stacks to building open-source, bottom-up intelligence models. In this exclusive interview recorded live at Cypher 2026, Vijay Shekhar Sharma sits down with Sudhi Sachdev to discuss why staying a passive AI user is a losing strategy, overcoming India's deficit of AI product managers and researchers, building Paytm's internal AI lab (Neb), monetizing agentic AI workflows across coding and workforce operations, applying vertical AI models to national priorities like agriculture and healthcare, and his personal commitment to angel-fund early-stage Indian AI builders. items.title: Stop Brain Drain: The Strategy to Build Deep Tech in India
items.summary: While Indian academic institutions generate world-class deep-tech research, translating lab-stage innovations into viable, commercialized market products remains a key hurdle. Established under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs) at premier institutes like IIT Bombay bridge this gap by funding seed-stage startups, advancing physical AI systems, and converting academic intellectual property into industry-ready solutions. In this interview recorded live at Cypher 2026, Sudhi Sachdev speaks with Dhruti Pillai, Assistant Vice President (AVP) of Technology at TIH, IIT Bombay. They explore reversing the traditional tech "brain drain" in favor of indigenous innovation, funding early-stage founders in physical AI, navigating enterprise procurement and corporate adoption risks, balancing ground-level reality with government policy, and leveraging frugal innovation to build sovereign technology capabilities for India. How do university innovation hubs convert cutting-edge academic research into market-ready deep-tech enterprises? ✅ Cypher 2026: Join 5,000+ AI leaders. In this interview recorded live at Cypher 2026, Sudhi Sachdev speaks with Dhruti Pillai, Assistant Vice President (AVP) of Technology at TIH, IIT Bombay. They explore reversing the traditional tech "brain drain" in favor of indigenous innovation, funding early-stage founders in physical AI, navigating enterprise procurement and corporate adoption risks, balancing ground-level reality with government policy, and leveraging frugal innovation to build sovereign technology capabilities for India.

How do university innovation hubs convert cutting-edge academic research into market-ready deep-tech enterprises?

items.title: LLM Applications: Conversational AI, Document Intelligence & Text-to-SQL
items.summary: Language models are not just a chat technology. The same capability reads your documents and queries your databases. Terms covered: - Conversational AI: multi-turn dialogue that remembers context, handles follow-ups, adapts to intent and escalates when it hits its limits - Document Extraction: pulling structured information out of contracts, invoices, claims, medical records and filings, in seconds instead of hours - Text-to-SQL: asking a database a question in plain English and getting the answer back, with no technical intermediary and no waiting on a data team Conversation, documents and data.
